en.title: Meetings and e-mails
en.summary: Organising a meeting and writing a clear, polite work e-mail.

paragraphs: At work you often have to arrange meetings and write e-mails. This lesson shows you the structure of a formal e-mail and the phrases for suggesting a time.
Rita and Alan are colleagues in a company in Cardiff, and they want to meet to discuss the budget.

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.text: Could we meet on Thursday to discuss the budget?

lines.speaker: Alan
lines.text: Thursday is difficult. I'm visiting a client all day. How about Friday at ten?

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.text: Friday is fine. I will send an invitation.

lines.speaker: Alan
lines.text: Thanks. Please include the agenda, so that everyone can prepare.

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.text: Of course. Shall I book a meeting room?

lines.speaker: Alan
lines.text: Yes, the small one on the second floor. We will only be four.

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.text: Perfect. I will also ask Dan to bring the figures.

paragraphs: **1. Could and would make requests polite.** In work e-mails, Could you... and Would you mind...-ing are softer than a command. See Introduction to Grammar: Moods, command, subjunctive and conditional.

blocks.html:
DirectPolite
Send me the report.Could you send me the report?
Call me.Would you mind calling me?
Tell me the time.Could you let me know the time?
Come at ten.Would ten o'clock suit you?

paragraphs: **2. E-mail phrases are fixed.** Learn the opening, the reason and the closing as units. See Introduction to Grammar: Sentence structure.

blocks.html:
PartPhrase
openingDear Ms Clark,
reasonI am writing to ask about...
requestI would be grateful if you could...
closingI look forward to hearing from you. Kind regards,

items: Attached means a file is sent with the message; Cc sends a copy to other people.
An agenda lists the points to discuss at the meeting.
Minutes are the written record of what was decided.
Suit you means be convenient for you.

paragraphs: Workplace e-mail in English is usually brief and polite, and a clear subject line helps. One request per message is easier to answer than several.
